Simply saying that this game is weird is not enough.
It's one of those franchises that looked weird as idea. On paper. As a prototype. As the first game. Second. Third and so on. It's a franchise that stays stubbornly, almost zealously close to original, throughout all those years, with barely any major overhauls and improvements. Clinging to the same niche formula that got lucky back in the day.

And yet somehow it stays fun.

[h3]Story - 4/10[/h3]
It's... as barebones and ridiculous as it looks. The Earth gets invaded by some giant monsters. Which look ridiculously like overgrown, Earth insects, yet everyone never addresses the elephant in the room, just referring to them as "monsters". And going ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy when spider-looking monsters shoot webs, or wasp-looking ones start flying. Later on - PLOT TWIST - they're made by aliens who use them as a vanguard for their invasion.
The whole story of the game are just dozens of missions that have you fight through progressively bigger, scarier hordes of those monsters. Occasionally they'll throw something at you that you can't normally overcome, and then you'll have to wait till HQ comes up with some solution. That's... kind of it. The Earth population slowly getting eradicated and you're trying to fight back.

[h3]Gameplay - 7.5/10[/h3]
The strongest selling point of the game, and the only thing that keeps the franchise alive. It's a horde shooter with almost full destructibility, dismemberment, enemies that actually react accordingly to you blowing off their limbs or other parts, and continuing to resist without them.
You have a choice between four classes, each of which almost has you playing four different games.
[list]
[*] Ranger offers the most classic, all-rounder, third person shooter experience. You're an ordinary soldier with a gun, here to shoot the bastards and try not to die. Kind of like discount Helldivers, just without the stratagems.
[*] Wing Divers are flying glass cannons. These ladies get the weapons with highest DPS and best ammo economy, but ultimately have only their mobility as their defense mechanism. Playing as them has you spending 99% of your time off the ground, raining hell from above and zooming around when you wish to live.
[*] Air Raider - yeah, speaking of raining hell - those are the Helldivers who got ONLY the stratagems. They did get some gun for self defense, but their main contribution to the team comes from all the air- and orbital-strikes that they can call in from safe distance. A class meant for those who want to watch the world burn.
[*] Fencer - the most unique class, which turns the game into a discount Armored Core. A soldier with a heavy exoskeleton, two switchable weapons per each hand, and arguably the most diverse gear to choose from. You can focus entirely on melee weapons and give yourself so many dashes and jumps that you'll be as mobile as Wing Divers. Or you can turn yourself into a slow, heavy artillery/tank, with heavy cannons and a bunch of cluster missiles with a lock-on.
[/list]
The biggest issue with the gameplay is progression - it's almost completely random, and some of those randomly unlockable weapons can really simplify the game for you. Or make you suffer without them, if you're unlucky.

[h3]Graphics - 5/10[/h3]
Yes, I get the "why." I really do - the game is such a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of calculations that barely any engine could even handle it without framerate drops (not that this game doesn't have them). But yes, the full destructibility and the sheer amount of monsters (and your NPC troops)  on screen, sadly, comes at a price. The game looks like it came from 2000s. Not "gauge your eyes out" levels of dated, but still very old looking.

[h3]Sound - 7/10[/h3]
The voice acting is over the top, typical anime-style, but trying to take itself overly serious. The SFX is decent, especially given the sheer amount of everything happening on screen. The soundtrack fits the ridiculous atmosphere well enough. The best part are the cadences, though. The fact that you can start singing any line from the EDF marching song and every NPC nearby will immediately catch up and sing along with you - never gets old.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
6/10. [Final thoughts]
"Niche" doesn't begin to describe it. But bought at a discount and enjoyed with full party of friends - it can definitely get addictive. At least enough to fully beat the campaign once.

Fantastic multiplayer game. Absolute mayhem. Someone described this as a game that looks like it was dreamt up by a 13-year-old boy ("let's have giant ants that crawl over skyscrapers but-but you can shoot at the skyscrapers with like a huge rocket launcher and then-then the skyscraper explodes!!!") and implemented by a professional studio -- and I agree with that description completely.
Lots of enemies and lots of awesome guns to shoot them with. Over the top in all the best ways.
